productionSuitable.description: Set to false for modules whose implementation is inherently unsuitable for production (e.g. a dev-mode server). Checked by CDS-SEC-073 against profiles declaring a non-local environment.

requiredIf.description: Dotted 'config.<path>==<value>' expression (same vocabulary as the renderer's enabledFrom equality gate); when it evaluates true against the module instance's own config, this consume entry is treated as required even if required is false, and a missing/invalid binding raises E041 at validate time instead of only surfacing later at render (E071) or container start. Must match config.<path>==<value> (dotted path, then a literal ==, then a non-empty value) so a typo fails at schema validation instead of silently disabling enforcement.

tls.description: TLS requirement for the bound provider (issue #577). 'required': the provider's contract spec must advertise a TLS-protected endpoint (a boolean 'tls: true' in its provides entry's contract spec, or a pure ${config.<path>} reference resolving to true against the producer instance's profile config); anything else -- an absent field, tls: false, or an unresolvable config reference -- fails validation with E128. An omitted tls key places no TLS requirement (backward compatible: existing profiles and module.yaml documents stay valid unless they explicitly opt into stricter TLS). Values other than 'required' are rejected at module schema validation (E021) so a typo cannot silently disable the check.

engineFrom.description: Engine requirement for the bound sql-database provider (issue #682). Dotted 'spec.config.<path>' reference to a string field in this module's own config holding the database engine/wire-protocol vendor the consumer expects the provider to speak (e.g. spec.config.metadataDatabase.driver in identity/keycloak, feeding KC_DB). At validate time the referenced value -- taken from the profile config when set, otherwise from the module configSchema default at that path -- is compared case-insensitively with the provider contract spec's advertised 'engine' (a literal string, or a pure ${config.<path>} reference resolving against the producer instance's profile config); a mismatch, or a provider that advertises no engine at all, fails validation with E154 so a wrong-vendor binding fails loudly instead of silently misconfiguring the consumer. An omitted engineFrom key places no engine requirement (backward compatible). Must match spec.config.<path> (dotted path under spec.config) so a typo fails at schema validation (E021) instead of silently disabling enforcement.

kind.description: Primary implementation kind. Retained for backward compatibility; 'targets' is authoritative when present.

targets.description: Render targets this module supports. Defaults to [kind] when omitted.

kubernetesImplementation.description: Kubernetes orchestration shape. Container-level detail (image, command, env, healthcheck, tmpfs, hardening flags) is translated from the compose fragment; this block declares only what compose cannot express. At least one of workloads or manifests must be present: a manifests-only module is render-only (no pods of its own), e.g. a GitOps bootstrap module.

workloads.description: Workload name -> spec. Each groups one or more compose services into a single Pod.

manifests.description: Manifest name -> raw Kubernetes manifest. Emitted verbatim (after ${...} substitution) as an extra chart template, for CRDs the workload model cannot express (e.g. FluxCD GitRepository/Kustomization/HelmRelease in a GitOps module). metadata.name is prefixed with the Helm release name unless it already contains a {{ .Release.Name }} template.

volumes.description: Classification of compose named volumes. Unlisted volumes become emptyDir.

configMaps.description: Bind-mounted files promoted to ConfigMaps, keyed by the compose bind source path.

services.description: Services the module's own manifests (or the operator they drive) cause to exist in the release namespace, e.g. the <cluster>-rw Service a CloudNativePG Cluster creates (issue #768). Declared but NOT rendered by CDS: the names join the renderer's service registry, so contract-host validation (E084/E150), release-scoped binding hosts, ${k8s.service.*}, and waitFor gates treat them exactly like rendered workload Services. Key naming follows the workload rule: key "rw" on module instance "warehouse" is "warehouse-rw" (release-scoped "{{ .Release.Name }}-warehouse-rw").

operators.description: Out-of-band operators the module's manifests depend on (issue #768). CDS renders the CRs but never installs the operator: `cds render`/`cds test` warn with W130 naming the operator and its install command, the chart's NOTES.txt lists it, and `cds up --target helm` fails closed with E155 when the operator's CRD is absent from the cluster. Each entry names the CRD the operator provides (`crd`, checked with `kubectl get crd`), a one-line `install` command, and an optional `docs` URL.

crd.description: A CRD the operator installs (e.g. "clusters.postgresql.cnpg.io"); `cds up --target helm` checks for it with `kubectl get crd` before installing the chart.

install.description: One-line command that installs the operator on the cluster, e.g. "helm repo add cnpg https://cloudnative-pg.github.io/charts && helm upgrade --install cnpg --namespace cnpg-system --create-namespace cnpg/cloudnative-pg".

docs.description: Optional documentation URL for the operator installation.

kubernetesOperator.description: An operator that must be installed on the cluster out of band before the module's manifests can be applied.

serviceName.description: Override the generated DNS name. Defaults to the module-prefixed key (same rule as workloads).

description.description: Why this Service exists and who creates it (e.g. an operator-created Service from a Cluster CR).

kubernetesDeclaredService.description: A Service the module does not render itself but expects to exist in the release namespace once its manifests are applied.

name.description: Object name. The helm renderer prefixes it with "{{ .Release.Name }}-" unless the name already contains a {{ .Release.Name }} template. May reference ${service.host} for the module instance id.

enabledFrom.description: Optional config path expression gating the manifest (e.g. "config.mode==chart"); the manifest is skipped when the expression resolves to False. Stripped from the rendered output.

kubernetesManifest.description: A raw Kubernetes manifest (any CRD) emitted as an extra chart template. Values support the same ${config.*}/${bindings.*}/${service.*}/${k8s.service.*} substitution as workloads. A value that is exactly one ${secrets.*} reference (resolving to ${CDS_*}) is rewritten to a Helm `required` lookup of .Values.secrets, so the secret value is supplied at install time and never stored in the chart; any other leftover ${CDS_*} is rejected by the renderer (E078) because chart files must never carry secret material.

kubernetesNetworkPolicy.description: Custom allow rules merged verbatim into the module's generated NetworkPolicy (issue #75). The generated policy is default-deny for ingress and egress; these rules exist because contract bindings cannot name external endpoints (e.g. an external API a job reads from) or cross-namespace clients (e.g. an ingress controller fronting a ClusterIP service), which would otherwise be silently denied.

egress.description: Additional NetworkPolicy egress rules (networking.k8s.io/v1 rule objects), rendered verbatim after the binding-derived rules. Scope each rule to the minimum: a specific ipBlock cidr or a namespace/pod selector peer, and a TCP port list; the security scan reports every external-egress rule as a low finding (CDS-K8S-008).

ingress.description: Additional NetworkPolicy ingress rules (networking.k8s.io/v1 rule objects), rendered verbatim after the binding-derived rules, e.g. to admit a cross-namespace ingress controller that no contract binding can name.

kubernetesEgress.description: Declared external egress destinations (issue #1023). The generated NetworkPolicy is default-deny for egress, and contract bindings are the only other source of allow rules, so egress to anything outside the plan -- an external database, an HTTPS API, a package index, an object store reached by address -- is denied unless declared here. Each entry renders as an ipBlock rule scoped to exactly the declared destination, except-CIDRs, and ports; undeclared external egress remains denied. Module-level entries apply to all of the module's pods; workload-level entries (workloads.<name>.egress) render as an additional workload-scoped NetworkPolicy. Broad declarations (0.0.0.0/0, or no port list) are reported by the security scan as CDS-K8S-009.

kubernetesEgressEntry.description: One external egress destination. Values support the same ${config.*} substitution as the rest of the kubernetes block, so a profile can supply the destination through module config; the renderer validates the resolved value and fails closed with E153. A DNS name is rejected: a NetworkPolicy cannot express one.

host.description: External destination as an IP literal (IPv4 or IPv6); rendered as a /32 or /128 ipBlock cidr.

cidr.description: External destination range as a CIDR block, rendered as an ipBlock cidr. Host bits must not be set (e.g. 10.20.0.0/16, not 10.20.0.5/16).

except.description: CIDRs inside cidr that stay denied (ipBlock.except); each must be a subnet of cidr.

port.description: Single destination port. Merged with ports when both are given.

oneOf.description: Config expression resolving to a list of port integers.

ports.description: Destination ports. When neither port nor ports is given the rule covers all ports to the destination (flagged by CDS-K8S-009).

protocol.description: Transport protocol for the declared ports.

kubernetesServiceAccount.description: Settings for the module's generated ServiceAccount. The ServiceAccount is always created; RBAC rules are optional and empty by default (least privilege).

rbac.description: RBAC rules granted to the module's ServiceAccount via a generated Role and RoleBinding. No rules means no API access and no mounted token.

kubernetesRbacRule.description: One rbac.authorization.k8s.io rule, rendered verbatim into the module's Role.

apiGroups.description: API groups the rule applies to, e.g. [""] for the core group.

resources.description: Resources the rule applies to, e.g. ["pods"].

resourceNames.description: Optional allowlist restricting the rule to named resource instances.

containers.description: Compose service names that become containers in this Pod.

initContainers.description: Compose service names that run to completion before the main containers start.

waitFor.description: Dependency gates rendered as wait initContainers, replacing compose depends_on conditions.

containerOverrides.description: Container name -> overrides applied after the compose fragment is translated.

serviceName.description: Override the generated Service/DNS name. Defaults to the module-prefixed workload name.

podSecurityContext.description: Pod-level securityContext. Needed where compose names a user (user: postgres) that Kubernetes can only express numerically.

egress.description: External egress destinations declared for this workload's pods only. Rendered as a separate workload-scoped NetworkPolicy (additive to the module policy); the module-level implementation.kubernetes.egress applies to all module pods.

size.description: PVC size, e.g. 5Gi. Required for persistentVolumeClaim.

sizeFrom.description: Config expression yielding the PVC size, e.g. config.storage.size.

kubernetesConfigMap.description: A file projected into containers as a ConfigMap. Source is either a compose bind path (fromBind) or inline content.

key.description: ConfigMap data key, normally the file basename.

fromBind.description: Compose bind source path whose file contents become the ConfigMap value.

content.description: Inline file content, used when no compose bind mount carries this file.

mountPath.description: Absolute path the file is projected to. Derived from the bind target when omitted.

containers.description: Containers that mount this file. Defaults to every container in the module.

mode.description: Octal file mode, e.g. 0555 for an executable script.

enabledFrom.description: Optional config path expression gating the ConfigMap (e.g. "config.sampleData.enabled"); when it resolves to False the ConfigMap is not rendered and its matching compose bind mounts are skipped on the Kubernetes target. Stripped from the rendered output.

timeoutSeconds.description: Hard deadline for one dependency wait attempt.

dropVolumeMounts.description: Compose volume/bind targets to NOT mount in Kubernetes (e.g. a Unix socket volume replaced by TCP).

dropProbes.description: Probes translated from the compose healthcheck that do not apply in Kubernetes (e.g. a Unix-socket check replaced by TCP).

securityContext.description: Merged over the securityContext derived from the compose hardening flags.

entrypoint.description: Overrides the compose entrypoint, which becomes the Kubernetes command.
